dimensions.rationale: The union includes all certifying bodies explicitly named in state statutes as recognized for advanced podiatric surgery or ankle surgery privileges; ABFAS and ABPS are kept separate because states treat them as distinct (ABPS is an older name and ABFAS its renamed/successor form, but multiple states reference both); ABPM and its predecessor 'American Board of Podiatric Orthopedics and Primary Podiatric Medicine' are merged; orthopedic surgery boards (ABOS and its osteopathic counterpart) are included because several states allow ankle surgery under supervision of an ABOS/osteopathic-board-certified physician as an alternative pathway; general medical specialty boards (ABMS, AOA Bureau) and non-podiatric bodies appearing only in unrelated contexts are excluded as they are not certifying bodies for podiatric ankle surgery privileges.
